title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input Sanitization and Deterministic Verification
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within an orchestration adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.7447%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration wording vs the formal estimand, document pipeline semantics and shared_initial_candidate reuse, disclose a protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature), and discuss operational interpretation and limitations constrained by synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts (execution manifest [14]).

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) show promise for automating NetOps tasks by translating high-level operator intent into device CLI. However, automated generation risks producing syntactic or semantic errors (ordering, preconditions, protected-interface violations) that can render configurations unsafe or non-deployable. Deterministic verifiers that operate over explicit network and configuration models (e.g., header-space approaches and VeriFlow-style tools) are natural deployment gates because they evaluate semantics (reachability, precedence, required sequences) rather than surface string similarity [5–7]. Motivated by these operational priorities and gaps in prior LLM evaluations that emphasize token- or reference-match metrics [3,8,9], we preregistered a narrowly scoped confirmatory question: in a paired design with shared_initial_candidate semantics, do template-based input sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) change the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents? The preregistration defined a single formal estimand—paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline—and a single confirmatory exact two-sided McNemar test, enabling a focused artifact-backed inference.
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-verification tools provide fast, semantics-oriented checks appropriate for pre-deployment gating and have been applied to forwarding and access-control invariants [5–7,14]. Empirical studies of LLMs for network configuration consistently report syntax and higher-level semantic failures in model-only outputs; these failures motivate integrating verifiers and constrained repair into orchestration loops [3,8,9,11]. Generate–validate–repair architectures have shown prototype benefits when verifier diagnostics are precise and repair scope is bounded [11,3]. Security work on prompt-injection and indirect prompt attacks demonstrates that multi-source pipelines are vulnerable unless inputs are sanitized and gating policies are strict [10,30]. Surveys and benchmark efforts call for operationally meaningful, validator-centered metrics (deployability/validator acceptance) rather than lexical-match scores [4,9,39]. Our study positions a preregistered estimator that uses deterministic-validator acceptance as the primary operational metric and explicitly enforces shared_initial_candidate semantics so that downstream sanitization/gating/repair are the causal factors under test.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and estimand. Study cand-2026-03 was preregistered before observing outcomes; the primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (paired difference in validator acceptance probabilities). The preregistered confirmatory test is the exact two-sided McNemar; paired 95% bootstrap percentile CIs use 10,000 resamples (seed = 1729). Design and task bank. The synthetic intent bank comprises deterministic templates exercising common NetOps workflows (interface admin, MTU, VLAN, protected-interface constraints, and required sequences). An adversary model applied deterministic mutation heuristics to these templates; generation seeds and mutation taxonomy are archived in the execution manifest. Model, validator, and orchestration. The declared generator was gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5; orchestration used a hosted generate–validate–repair adapter implementing a guarded pipeline. The guarded branch applied template-based sanitization and a policy permitting at-most-one automated repair. Pipeline semantics and shared_initial_candidate. Because generation semantics were registered as shared_initial_candidate, each paired unit used a single LLM draft for both Baseline and Guarded scoring. The per-pair timeline was: (1) task instantiation and adversarial mutation; (2) single shared initial generation call producing the shared_initial_candidate used by both conditions; (3) Baseline scoring: deterministic validator applied to the shared draft; (4) Guarded branch: sanitizer applied and, if the policy allowed, at-most-one repair LLM call permitted; (5) final validation of the sanitized or repaired candidate. This design isolates downstream guarded-pipeline effects (sanitization, gating, permitted repair, final validation) from differences in initial generation. Missingness, exclusions, and analysis plan. The preregistered missingness plan excludes a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures. Planned episodes = 300; completed = 282; complete pairs included in primary analysis = 141. Primary analysis used paired_binary_analysis_v1 (exact McNemar) and the specified bootstrap CI parameters recorded in the archived analysis artifacts.
sections.results: Execution and counts. The run completed 282 of 300 planned episodes; 18 episodes failed for technical reasons and were handled per the preregistered exclusion rule, yielding 141 complete pairs. Provider-call accounting recorded model_calls_used = 156 total model-call events (147 completed, 9 failed); stage counts show shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair-stage events = 6. Condition-level outcomes and paired contingency. Baseline successes = 135/141 (0.9574468085106383); Guarded successes = 141/141 (1.0). The paired contingency table is n11 = 135, n10 = 6 (guarded-only successes), n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Inference and interval estimates. The preregistered exact two-sided McNemar test yields p = 0.03125 for the paired comparison (Guarded vs Baseline). Observed paired estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. The 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. Discordant-case diagnostics. The six n10 discordant pairs are traceable in the archived per-episode validator traces; reconciliation links each discordant pair to sanitizer normalization and/or a single permitted repair that converted a draft the baseline validator rejected into a final candidate the validator accepted. Conservative sensitivity. Treating the nine both-missing pairs as failures (sensitivity, not preregistered primary) yields baseline acceptance = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded acceptance = 141/150 = 0.9400, showing the observed direction persists under this conservative assumption. All numeric results, per-pair traces, and reconciliation artifacts are archived and cited in the execution manifest [14].
sections.discussion: Estimand interpretation and reconciliation. The preregistration's natural-language H1 framed verifier-gating as reducing attacker success; the formal registered estimand measured paired validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). These differ substantively: an increase in validator acceptance under the guarded pipeline may reflect successful recovery of reparable drafts (benign drafts fixed) rather than decreased attacker success under adversary-centric definitions. Our empirical result—an absolute increase of ≈4.255 percentage points (p = 0.03125)—arose because sanitizer normalization and bounded repair recovered drafts that the baseline validator rejected. Consequently, the formal-estimand improvement should not be interpreted as an attacker-centric safety reduction without an independent semantic-safety oracle. Operational implications. Within the synthetic setting and the validator's encoded coverage, template-based sanitization plus bounded repair reduced rework by converting invalid drafts into validator-accepted candidates. This benefit critically depends on two co-design elements: (i) the validator's semantic coverage (what safety properties it encodes) and (ii) the allowed repair scope. The six discordant cases illustrate the operational tradeoff: repairs enabled acceptance but only preserve safety if they maintain original intent semantics. Therefore deployment requires joint specification of gating policies, repair limits, and validator expressiveness to avoid masking adversarial manipulations. Relation to prior work. Our results align with prototype generate–validate–repair demonstrations that integrating verifiers and constrained repair improves concrete outcome metrics on narrow tasks [11,3], and they respond to calls for validator-centered benchmarks and operational metrics [4,9]. They also highlight security concerns documented in prompt-injection literature: sanitization alone is insufficient absent verifier expressiveness and careful repair policy design [10,30]. Threats to validity and limitations. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample size; paired exclusions were applied per preregistered rules. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 encodes CLI grammar, required sequences, and protected-interface invariants but does not represent all dynamic protocol-level semantics; validator acceptance is therefore a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: a single generator (gpt-5-mini), single validator, and synthetic intent bank limit generalization. Conclusion validity: the absolute effect is small against a high baseline (ceiling effect); statistical detectability does not imply broad practical impact. Reproducibility guidance and protocol deviation. The archived model configuration recorded temperature = null (unset), which we disclose as a protocol deviation because provider-side defaults can affect sampling determinism; the run nevertheless preserved paired comparability via shared_initial_candidate semantics. Provider-call accounting shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 156 with 6 repair-stage events linked to the six discordant pairs. For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly setting temperature = 0 and re-executing the archived execution manifest; the manifest and analysis artifacts contain the complete run record and parameters required for reproduction (archive cited as [14]). Recommendations. (1) Execute the preregistered benign-control to measure false-positive blocking; (2) preregister and measure attacker-centric estimands that combine validator acceptance with an independent semantic-safety oracle; (3) diversify generators and validators across vendor CLIs and protocols; (4) fix sampling settings (temperature = 0) for deterministic reproduction; and (5) co-design repair policies and validator expressiveness to bound the risk that repairs mask adversarial intents.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank, template-based input sanitization plus deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference ≈ 0.04255; p = 0.03125; 95% CI [0.01418, 0.07801]). Diagnostics show the six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair calls that enabled acceptance. This formal-estimand improvement does not equate to a measured reduction in attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and a protocol deviation (unset runtime temperature). Future work should run the preregistered benign-control, evaluate attacker-centric estimands with independent semantic oracles, diversify models and validators, and set explicit sampling parameters for deterministic reproduction. All principal numbers and reconciliation claims above are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts; the execution manifest is the primary machine-verifiable archive and is cited below as [14].

limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
